requirements.text: The user guide must feature the plant owner's responsibility to secure the perimeter.

HART (IF-2) Maintenance-level write authentication shall use a credential mechanism at least as strong as the local HMI's (AS-2 role-credential model) and shall implement rate-limiting/lockout on repeated failed attempts equivalent to the local HMI's protection (AS-12), so the still-open choice of exact HART authentication mechanism cannot end up weaker than the already-decided HMI baseline.

The Ethernet service interface (IF-4) shall use TLS 1.2 or higher (or an equivalent authenticated, encrypted transport), with the device authenticating to the client via a device-unique certificate or key provisioned at manufacturing, validated using standard, non-deprecated cipher suites, and with certificate/hostname validation logic covered by dedicated test cases before release, closing AS-8's still-open protocol/cert-management choice to a concrete, testable minimum bar.

Protocol parsers for HART (IF-2), Modbus RTU (IF-3), and the Ethernet service interface (IF-4) shall be exercised with fuzz/malformed-input testing as part of the release process, with crashes, hangs, or undefined behavior on malformed input treated as release-blocking defects.

MCU debug/programming interfaces (JTAG/SWD, IF-7) shall be disabled or locked (readout protection enabled) in production firmware before a unit ships, per AS-17; if a factory-debug/recovery state is needed, it shall require the same Manufacturer-support-level authorization as bootloader/service-mode access (AS-1) and shall be irreversibly re-locked (or re-verified locked) before the unit leaves manufacturer control. The specific readout protection level and the recovery/debug procedure itself shall be documented and tested.

Firmware code-signing keys shall be generated, stored, and used under a documented key-management policy (e.g. HSM-backed, access restricted to named roles, dual control for key use, logged signing events), so that AS-3's signature-check protection is not undermined by weak protection of the signing key itself.

A vulnerability handling and patch-management process shall be maintained for the RL-100 product line (intake of reports/CVEs affecting the platform or third-party components, triage, target remediation timelines by severity, and customer notification), tracked per-defect in the 09-defects register.

A software bill of materials (SBOM) shall be maintained for third-party/OSS components used in the firmware (component, version, supplier, license, CPE/purl identifier), kept current across releases, to support the vulnerability-handling process (REQC008) with automated CVE matching.

Modbus RTU (IF-3) writes to operational configuration registers shall require a local confirmation step (e.g. HMI acknowledgement) or an explicit write-protect toggle before being applied, so a device sharing the RS-485 segment cannot silently change configuration without on-site interaction.

Firmware update images shall be verified via cryptographic signature and monotonic version/anti-rollback check before being applied, consistent with the already-implemented update-time verification (AS-3).

All cryptographic operations (firmware-signature verification, TLS on IF-4, key handling) shall use a validated, actively-maintained cryptographic library (e.g. mbedTLS, wolfSSL, or an equivalent vetted implementation) rather than a custom/in-house cryptographic primitive, including constant-time implementations for secret-dependent comparisons and operations, so that implementation-level weaknesses (timing side-channels, faulty signature-verification logic, weak random-number generation) are avoided by library selection and configuration rather than case-by-case detection.

Protocol-facing services on HART (IF-2), Modbus RTU (IF-3), and the Ethernet service interface (IF-4) shall enforce resource limits (e.g. maximum concurrent connections, request-rate limiting, bounded per-connection buffer/state allocation) so that a high volume of connection attempts or requests cannot exhaust firmware resources and deny service to legitimate use. This control shall be exercised with dedicated load/resource-exhaustion testing as part of the release process, with resource exhaustion, hangs, or crashes under sustained load treated as release-blocking defects.

Authenticated write-capable protocol interfaces (HART IF-2 per REQC003, and any future networked configuration interface) shall implement replay protection (e.g. a nonce or timestamp bound to each authenticated write) so that a captured legitimate write command cannot be replayed later to reproduce its effect.
